back: The energy of anything that is moving.
Stored energy an object has because it is raised up high, e.g. water behind a dam.
Stored energy in something stretched or squashed, e.g. a bungy cord or a spring.

front: Name the nine forms of energy
back: Kinetic, gravitational potential, elastic, chemical, thermal, electrical, light, sound, nuclear.
A change of energy from one form to another, e.g. a solar panel changes light into electrical energy.
Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed or transferred. The total stays the same.
It becomes heat (thermal energy) that spreads into the surroundings, often caused by friction.
Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ total energy in × 100%.

front: Energy flow in a hydro power station

back: Renewable sources are naturally replaced (hydro, geothermal, wind, solar). Non-renewable sources will run out (coal, oil, natural gas).
Hydro (more than half). Geothermal and wind are other important renewables.
Heat passing through a material as particles vibrate and pass energy on. Best in solids, especially metals.
Heat transfer in liquids and gases: warm fluid becomes less dense and rises, cooler fluid sinks, making a convection current.
Heat travelling as infrared waves. It needs no particles, so it can cross empty space.
A poor conductor of heat, e.g. wood, plastic, wool, polystyrene, trapped air.
